title: Answer After a Choice Instruction
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine, and suppose its instruction at state $l$ chooses between states $l_1$ and $l_0$. For any register valuation $v$, recorded answer $r$, natural number $N$, and Boolean value $b$, there is a length-$N+1$ choice sequence that leaves answer $b$ from the configuration $(l,v,r)$ if and only if such a length-$N$ sequence exists from at least one of $(l_1,v,r)$ or $(l_0,v,r)$.
hypotheses_covered: A(l) is the choice instruction with targets l₁ and l₀
